+/-- Tensoring the successive DVR quotient sequence with a flat-term complex is short exact.
+The second map is the recorded canonical quotient transition, before localization.
+
+Source: Stacks Project, sites-cohomology.tex, Tag 0942, proof of lemma-bounded,
+specialized to the principal ideal generated by a uniformizer; derived.tex, Tag 0152
+(blueprint: lem-sf-integral-reduction-flat-filtration).
+
+Proof: write R for the recorded valuation ring and pi for its nonzero uniformizer.
+For n >= 0, multiplication by pi^(n+1) gives an injective R-linear map
+R/(pi) -> R/(pi^(n+2)). It is well defined since pi*pi^(n+1)=pi^(n+2).
+Cancellation of the nonzero pi^(n+1) proves injectivity. Its image is the kernel
+of R/(pi^(n+2)) -> R/(pi^(n+1)), and the latter map is surjective by choosing
+representatives. Sheafify this constant-module sequence on the pro-etale site.
+Exactness of associated sheaves gives a short exact sequence of coefficient sheaves.
+Regard them as modules over the completed coefficient sheaf B via its projections.
+The injection is B-linear: projection compatibility identifies the image of a
+section of B modulo pi with its higher projection modulo pi; multiplying their
+difference by pi^(n+1) kills it modulo pi^(n+2). This identity can be checked
+locally on constant sections. The quotient map is B-linear by the same projection
+compatibility. Tensor this short exact sequence with each flat term P.X j.
+Flatness preserves finite limits and colimits, hence its short exactness.
+The maps commute with the differentials by functoriality of tensoring.
+The tensor terms are precisely integralTowerComplex at indices 0, n+1, n:
+the balancing map sends pi^r tensor x to pi^r tensor x in the restricted
+change-of-rings sheafification. Its inverse is the same formula. The second
+chain map sends s tensor x to rho(s) tensor x, so uniqueness in
+integralTowerMaps_existUnique identifies it with integralTowerTransition.
+Finally, short exactness of cochain complexes is degreewise short exactness.
+This includes n=0 (the pi^2 quotient sequence), the zero complex, and the empty site. -/
